limitation: Windows PowerShell 5.1, real registry/COM shortcut writes, tray shutdown and Windows file locks still need the Windows PC.
method: Production setup/uninstall executed in small isolated filesystem fixtures; Windows registry, shell and process boundaries mocked.
results: First install preserves unrelated startup entries and writes an ownership marker
Update preserves saved data and startup preference on
Update preserves saved data and startup preference off
Unknown pre-existing folder is rejected without changing files or registry
Wrong ownership marker is rejected without changing files
Malformed ownership marker is rejected: arrayMarker
Malformed ownership marker is rejected: stringSchema
A blank pre-existing native host default is preserved and rejected
Linked directories inside an owned installation are rejected before traversal or deletion
New folder appearing during setup cannot receive or lose staged files
First-install shortcut failure rolls back app and own registry values
Update failure restores old files, data, startup and exact shortcut bytes
Rollback preserves existing native host keys with unrelated values and no default
A blocked file rollback retains the old backup and still restores registry and shortcut
Failure to launch after commit preserves the completed installation
Owned uninstall removes only owned files, registration, shortcut and startup
Uninstall rejects an unknown folder before touching registrations or files
Setup rejects a different startup command containing the expected app path
Uninstall preserves a different startup command containing the expected app path
Concurrent setup/uninstall processes cannot acquire the same installation lock
